headline: South Korean police opened an early inquiry into information leaks that hit several major banks at the same time, which Chosunbiz describes as AI hacking attacks.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: four major banks and a police inquiry, though the article gives no scale of the leak.
importance_line: What changed: police have stepped in after hacking damage was officially confirmed at several major banks, including four named in the report, which affects bank customers first, then the banks and regulators, and the doubt is that no figures on what data was taken are given, and "AI hacking attacks" is Chosunbiz's own description.
summary: Chosunbiz reports that South Korea's national police cyber unit began a preliminary inquiry on 2 Oct 2026 into simultaneous information leaks at banks including Shinhan, KB Kookmin, Hana and BNK Busan, which the outlet describes as AI hacking attacks. New since the 1 Oct 2026 report of a Shinhan Bank leak: police are now involved, and a formal case would be the first major cyber case under the revised Criminal Procedure Act that took effect the same day.
notes: Follow-up of 1002:C12-06 (Korea Herald, Shinhan Bank leak, 1 Oct 2026). New today: police inquiry and official confirmation of damage at four banks. The article gives no customer numbers.
